Polymorphs in chemistry refer to different crystal structures of the same chemical compound. They have the same chemical composition but differ in their physical properties due to different arrangements of atoms in the crystal lattice.

Let's analyze each option:

A. Physical attributes like melting points - Polymorphs typically have different melting points because the different crystal structures require different amounts of energy to break down. So this characteristic changes between polymorphs.

B. The nature of intermolecular interactions - Polymorphs have different arrangements of molecules in the crystal structure, which means the intermolecular interactions (hydrogen bonding, van der Waals forces, etc.) are different. So this characteristic changes between polymorphs.

C. Their chemical formulae - Polymorphs have the same chemical composition and formula. They are the same compound, just arranged differently in the solid state. This characteristic remains unchanged between polymorphs.

D. Torsional angles - Polymorphs often have different torsional angles as the molecules can adopt different conformations in different crystal structures. So this characteristic changes between polymorphs.

Based on this analysis, the characteristic that typically remains unchanged between two polymorphs of a compound is their chemical formula.
